title: Studio calls and film appearances with Armstrong
summary: He did a little studio work with Armstrong and pickup bands and appeared briefly in pictures, with D. W. Griffith and other directors visiting the club.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: But when you went to -- left the Cotton Club and went to the Apex, were you still doing studio work?

No, not -- we were traveling mostly. We did very little studio work from the Apex. I did a little studio work with Armstrong. We made a couple of pictures. I can't even think of the names.* And, you know, like I say, we'd get the calls, the studios calls used to come in any time. Different fellows would get a call for a band, or thrown together band, put together outfit. See, everybody usually knew the
tunes, so you'd just go out and play. And we did quite a bit of that until the whole idea finally gave out and we didn't do it anymore.
Were you ever on camera in any of these?
Passing. You know how the camera sweeps around. Yeah, we've been on some of those.
Yes, we did a pictures, some kind of races, horse race picture.
"A Day at the Races," with the Marx Brothers, I think it was. But -- oh, and I made -- it was Janet Gaynor and one of those "Seventh Heaven" pictures.
I forget so many of them.
Yes, way back. And we used to -- people like D. W. Griffith, and all those big directors used to frequent the club all the time. And oh, it was a gorgeous life in those days. Beautiful.
